founding_year.basis: The firm's own release of 1999-04-20: 'Rolf Mathies, Dr. Christian Nagel und Dr. Hendrik Brandis gruendeten Earlybird'; its site: 'Founded in 1997 ... born in Hamburg, Germany in 1997'.

history.value: Earlybird was founded in Hamburg in 1997 by Hendrik Brandis, Christian Nagel and Rolf Mathies, and today works from Berlin and Munich. It became known for early bets on Interhyp, N26, Isar Aerospace, Aleph Alpha and Black Forest Labs. In 2026 it closed its eighth early stage fund at €360 million and says it manages €2.5 billion; the track record on this page leaves out the former Digital East fund, now Bek Ventures.
history.basis: Founding: Hamburg 1997, three founders (the firm's release of 1999-04-20; Roland Manger joined in December 1998 as fourth partner and the firm calls him a co-founder today). Offices: Hamburg and Munich by 1999, Hamburg closed December 2011 and the team moved to Berlin; principal office Berlin, second office Munich. The bets named are companies in the portfolio on this page (Interhyp seed 1999, N26 seed 2014, Isar Aerospace Series A 2019, Aleph Alpha Series A 2021, Black Forest Labs Series A 2024). Fund VIII: EUR 360M, announced 2026-04-30 (the firm's own post). EUR 2.5 billion: the firm's own statement (homepage; E2D release 2026-06-18). Left out of the page text and kept here: the Digital East Fund operated under the licensed Earlybird brand from 2012 to August 2024 and now trades as Bek Ventures (Vestbee 2024-11-13); its companies, UiPath and Payhawk among them, are not in the portfolio on this page (decisions.md D2). Earlybird Health (Cologne-managed, Health I EUR 85M, Health II EUR 173M) and Earlybird-X (the EUR 75M university fund of 2021) are included. Also not on the page: 9 IPOs and 41 trade sales by the firm's own count (the nine include UiPath); the first two funds raised DM 85M together in 1999, Earlybird III was launched at $250M in 2000.

investment_concept.basis: The firm's own statement: the homepage headline, three h1 lines 'YOUR PARTNERS / FROM BEFORE / THE BREAKTHROUGH', read 2026-10-06, set in sentence case with one closing period. Competing lines on the site: 'Earlybird backs Pre-Seed to Series A founders in emerging tech - from fintech to nuclear fusion.' (homepage) and the meta description 'Founded in 1997, Earlybird is a pan-European VC investor backing tech-enabled companies ...'.

investment_stage.basis: The firm's own words: 'Earlybird backs Pre-Seed to Series A founders'; the homepage gives the split Pre-Seed 20%, Seed 60%, Series A 20%. Growth is added for the Growth Opportunities funds (initial tickets of EUR 10M to 15M at Series B and later, Unquote 2022) and Earlybird Health's Series B and C entries. The portfolio's cited entry rounds: Seed 54, Series A 54, Growth 16, Pre-Seed 16; 58 unnamed.

investment_geo.basis: The firm: 'Our roots are firmly in Europe, and we're driven to support the next generation of European founders'; 'a Pan-European VC with offices in Berlin, London, and Munich'. The portfolio's headquarters: Germany first, then the UK, Switzerland and France; a US minority (the 1999 to 2008 funds invested there, and a few recent US seeds).

investment_scope.basis: Generalist. The firm's own enumeration is 'Applications (B2B & B2C), Software Infrastructure, and DeepTech', with Earlybird Health for life sciences; its site tags do not map one to one onto the closed twelve, so the focus list is the portfolio's own distribution from the per-company classification (Healthcare & Bio 39, SaaS 25, Consumer & Marketplaces 24, AI & Applied AI 23, Industrial & Robotics 20, Fintech & Payments 16 companies), flagged derived.

investment_range.basis: Upper limit: the firm's own statement 'Initial ticket sizes up to EUR 12m' (homepage counter, read 2026-10-06): EUR 12.0M @ ECB 2026-10-06 (EUR/USD 1.1269) = $13,522,800; the Growth Opportunity funds write EUR 10M to 15M initial tickets (Unquote 2022), and the largest round the technology funds led alone is Gourmey's EUR 48M Series A (2022). Median: the size of the 15 entry rounds the firm announced between March 2024 and July 2026 (its own posts and tech.eu), median about $8M ($7.7M without the one Health Series C); a round-size proxy for the cheque, and Earlybird led or co-led every one, so entries where it only took part are not in the sample. Lower limit: the smallest of those entry rounds, Neuracore's $3M pre-seed (2025). The Form D leg does not apply: the firm's European companies file none. Press-based, flagged.

notable_investments.basis: The five best known of the firm's own companies, most recognised first (PRO-152). Considered next: Wunderlist (6Wunderkinder), Aiven, Tipp24, Peak Games, OneFootball. UiPath and Payhawk are not eligible: Digital East Fund positions, outside this portfolio (decisions.md D2).

aum.basis: Bottom: the sworn Form ADV Section 7.B(1) gross asset values of the exempt reporting adviser Earlybird GmbH & Co. KG (CRD 341941, filed 2026-05-19; sources/registers/adv-341941.txt): Fund VI $505,942,344; Fund VII $421,218,760; Growth Opportunities Fund V $169,568,893; Growth Opportunities Fund I $133,789,009; Fund VIII $119,181,384; Fund VI Affiliates $65,495,975 = $1,415,196,365. A floor: it leaves out Earlybird Health (its own manager in Cologne), Earlybird-X and every older fund. Top: the firm's own statement, 'EUR 2.5 billion under management across fund streams' (release of 2026-06-18; the April 2026 coverage itemises the early stage funds, five Growth Opportunity funds and Earlybird Health): EUR 2.50B @ ECB 2026-06-18 (EUR/USD 1.1461) = $2,865,250,000. Digital East left in August 2024; earlier statements that included it (over EUR 1B in 2019, EUR 2B in June 2022) are not used.

funds.basis: Sizes from the firm and the press, each converted at the ECB rate of its own date; no entry carries a Form D accession (Fund VIII's Form D of 2026-05-19 is a US notice, not the fund's size). Fund VIII EUR 360M (firm, 2026-04-30; 1.1702); Fund VII EUR 350M hard cap (TechCrunch 2022-05-17; 1.0541); Fund VI EUR 175M (VentureBeat, July 2018; month-end 1.1736); Earlybird 2012 EUR 150M (TechCrunch 2013-07-31; 1.3275); Earlybird IV EUR 127M (the firm's release of 2008-08-12; 1.4907); Health II EUR 173M and Health I (the Health Tech Fund) EUR 85M (TechCrunch 2024-02-14; 1.0713 for both, Health I's own close date is not on record); Growth Opportunity IV EUR 100M (Unquote, mid-2021; month-end 1.1884); UNI-X Seed Fund I EUR 75M (Gruenderszene 2021-10-11; 1.1574). Not listed for want of a size on record: the first two funds (DM 85M together, April 1999), Earlybird III (launched at $250M in January 2000, final size unknown), the debut Growth Opportunity fund of 2009, Growth Opportunities I and V (V had a EUR 300M target), Growth Fund VI and the Health Opportunities Fund (both registered 2024 to 2026, no announcement). Feeders, Team, Carry, Affiliates and holding vehicles are not funds. Digital East Fund 2013 SCA SICAR and Digital East Fund II are outside the firm (decisions.md D2).

hq_location.basis: Principal office on the newest Form ADV: C/O Earlybird Venture Capital Muenzstrasse 23, Berlin, Germany (EARLYBIRD GMBH & CO. KG, CRD 341941, SEC ERA Report filed 2026-05-19). The firm's site lists Berlin, Germany; London, United Kingdom; Milan, Italy; Munich, Germany; Hamburg, Germany; the principal office is among them, so the site agrees. Rule (Erik 2026-09-24): the newest Form ADV principal office, unless the firm's own site disagrees, and then the site wins.
